editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 30, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 29 commits today, 6.9 above its current daily pace, with 3 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 147 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
earendil-works/pi — No same-day commit, but 1 mapped article landed today. Preserve the mismatch and inspect the source window before following up.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Check which MCP implementation owns your Pi session
dailyInsight.insight: Pi v0.99 supplies MCP as a replaceable built-in extension. Existing adapters can retain the session command, while newer adapters can choose separate command and configuration names.
dailyInsight.mechanism: An extension registering /mcp displaces the built-in session integration. Nested tool calls can use common validation and call/result hooks; standalone pi mcp shell commands still use the built-in implementation.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: An upgrade can offer useful default connections without forcing the same ownership arrangement on every existing extension-based workflow.

actions.audience: Pi users upgrading a setup with an MCP extension
actions.label: Try one disposable read-only connection
actions.instruction: With a copy of the current configuration, identify which extension owns the session command, connect one read-only test server and check the expected tool and result hooks. Keep the previous setup available until the adapter and Pi versions work together.
actions.effort: One isolated session before migrating the working setup

receipts.title: Pi v0.99.0 supplies replaceable built-ins
receipts.supports: Publishes MCP, Code Mode and tool search with public nested-execution mechanisms.

receipts.title: Versioned replacement and SDK contract
receipts.supports: Documents session command ownership, the shell-command exception and explicit SDK extension loading.

confidence.basis: Release documentation, implementation and regression definitions agree on replacement and nested-call mechanisms.

dailyInsight.limitation: We inspected code and test definitions, not a live MCP integration. Adapter configuration migration does not prove compatibility between released versions; the VM does not confine invoked host tools.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A pinned release reproducer showing that the built-in connects a server despite replacement by an installed /mcp extension would contradict this ownership contract.
dailyInsight.watchNext: An extension migration that preserves command ownership, policy hooks and tool results against the released Pi interfaces.
